newsitem.title: USA: Clinton holds large lead in ABC, CBS polls.
newsitem.headline: Clinton holds large lead in ABC, CBS polls.

text.p: Bob Dole did better than expected in his first debate with President Clinton but the Republican presidential challenger failed to improve his standing in the latest ABC News poll released Wednesday.

The poll said 54 percent of registered voters in the poll taken Monday and Tuesday felt Dole did better than they had expected before Sunday's debate. But the pollsters said "that's mainly a sign they didn't expect much, since only 18 percent think he won it."
In contrast, 50 percent felt that Clinton won.

ABC News said among likely voters within the survey Clinton led Dole by 16 percentage points, 54 to 38 percent, with 5 percent favouring Reform Party candidate Ross Perot if the election were held now.

In a CBS News poll of 973 registered voters released Wednesday, but also taken Monday and Tuesday, had the Clinton-Al Gore ticket up by an even larger margin -- 21 percentage points -- 56 to 35 percent, with Perot trailing at 5 percent. The poll had a margin of error of plus or minus 3 percentage points.
The race has been generally stable since Labour Day in the ABC poll.
The ABC poll sampled 1,005 registered voters and included 848 likely voters. It had a margin of error of plus or minus 3.5 and 4 percent respectively.

In the latest Reuters tracking poll Wednesday, Clinton moved up slightly to an 8.1 percentage point lead over Dole, 44.7 percent to 36.6 percent. Perot had 4.4 percent. from 5.3 percentage points Tuesday. Clinton had a 5.3 point lead on Tuesday.
